newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana companies set to win U.S. ship contracts.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana companies set to win U.S. ship contracts.

text.p: Waterman Steamship Corp and Central Gulf Lines of Louisiana will be awarded contracts to operate seven cargo ships for the U.S. government, Democratic Sen. John Breaux and Republican Rep. Bob Livingston said on Wednesday. Both lawmakers are from Louisiana.
Waterman will operate four ships and Central Gulf three. The contracts are for $2.1 million per ship each year through 2005.

The ships will be used to transport military supplies during a war or national emergency as part of the Maritime Security Program, which authorizes $100 million to maintain a fleet of 47 cargo vessels.
